tagline: Up the South Umpqua and home by South Myrtle Creek.
intro: From Canyonville, County Road 1 runs east up the South Umpqua past farms and old houses to Tiller, and South Umpqua Road carries on upriver. About six miles past Tiller, Forest Road 2810 turns off into old-growth Douglas fir, with glimpses of the Rogue-Umpqua Divide Wilderness, and then a steep, narrow road of one lane leads on to Red Top Pond.

From the pond the road widens and follows South Myrtle Creek for about 17 miles down through hills with cattle, sheep and wild turkeys to Myrtle Creek, named for the groves of Oregon myrtle that grow nearby.
season: TripCheck gives late spring for wildflowers and fall for color as the best times.

moments.title: Milo Academy Bridge
moments.text: When the academy replaced its wooden covered bridge with steel in 1962, residents missed the old one, so its covering went onto the new steel truss.

moments.title: Red Top Pond
moments.text: The steep one-lane road comes out at this reservoir, popular for fishing and picnicking, and from here the route widens again.

moments.title: Myrtle Creek
moments.text: In 1868 Letitia Carson won title to a homestead near here, one of the first 71 claims under the Homestead Act and the only one in Oregon by a Black woman.

practical: Parts of the route are single lane or gravel, and the steep one-lane section to Red Top Pond can be hazardous for motor homes and trailers and is often closed in winter.
